extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies that prepare documents for publication in the Federal Register (Office staff and Federal Register Liaison Officers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Federal agency staff on preparing, signing, formatting, and transmitting documents for publication in the Federal Register (rules, proposed rules, notices, and related filings). Covers headings, preambles, signatures, transmission methods, and category-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of must/should/may
rubrics_metrics.description: We use “must” to indicate a requirement. We use “should” to indicate a strong recommendation. We use “may” to indicate an option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document categories must not be combined
rubrics_metrics.description: No, the OFR does not accept any document for publication that combines material that would appear in different categories of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two categories are involved, submit two separate documents that cross-reference each other. You may request that the two documents be published in the same separate part of a Federal Register issue (see Appendix A: Special Handling Request). Example cross-reference language provided (Example 1-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jointly issued documents: signature and agency identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Your Liaison Officer should consult with OFR in advance when preparing common or jointly issued documents. Make sure an authorized official from each agency has signed a jointly issued or common rule document. Identify each agency in the heading and preamble of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry the agencies in numerical order by CFR title number in both the heading and regulatory text. All agencies should sign in the same place; do not separate multiple signatures. Examples of joint headings and formatting provided (Example 1-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Billing Address Code (BAC) required
rubrics_metrics.description: GPO assigns agencies a Billing Address Code (BAC). Your BAC must appear on each document submitted for publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type the BAC at the top of the first page of the original(s) and the certified copies. You may include multiple BACs on a jointly-issued document. Consult your Printing Officer, Federal Register Liaison, or financial unit if you do not know your BAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin each document with prescribed document headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin each document with headings that identify your agency and the subject matter of your document. Present the headings using the appropriate format and in the specified order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific instructions for the document category (Proposed Rules, Rules and Regulations, Notices). Table 1-1 lists required headings (with and without subagency). The headings shown in bold are required; italic headings may or may not be required depending on document type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department and Subagency heading rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The “Department” is the highest-level agency and appears in the headings even if the document is issued by a subagency. The “Subagency” heading is used only if your agency is part of a larger agency and has specific legal authority to publish in the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt whether to use a Subagency heading, check with your liaison. Subagencies are usually assigned a distinct billing code. Examples provided (Examples 1-3 through 1-6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject heading content and style
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject heading is a title that briefly and accurately describes the document’s subject matter. Do not use legal citations in this or other headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid language that states the document’s regulatory effect (e.g., “Amendments to…”, “Revisions to…”). Be concise; OFR may edit for style but otherwise uses the subject heading verbatim as the index entry. Long headings will truncate automatically which may change meaning. You may not add a footnote or endnote to a subject heading. For follow-up documents, duplicate earlier headings and add a distinguishing phrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of availability for non-incorporated references
rubrics_metrics.description: If you provide an informational reference to a publication that is not incorporated by reference, include a statement of availability which identifies the title, edition/date/year, author, and publisher; and contains information where to find the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include a website; if there is a relevant physical address and phone number, include those as well. If the reference is required to comply with the regulations, follow the IBR Handbook incorporation-by-reference requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signer authority and title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The signer must be a Federal employee with the authority to act for the agency. The title in the signature block must be related to the authority to sign the document. Do not include honorary titles or titles associated with a different agency role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR may require the agency to validate the title on agency letterhead and may reject documents with an invalid title. Contact fedreg.legal@nara.gov for questions about authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper signature format and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: For paper documents, the signature must be in ink; it cannot be from an image file or a photocopy. Type the name and title of the person signing directly beneath the handwritten signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blue ink recommended to distinguish from photocopies. Do not place a signature block on a page by itself. Placing text on the signature page helps ensure integrity. We will reject documents signed as one person for another (signing someone else's name with your initials). Autopen is allowed in place of a wet signature but images of signatures are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital signature requirements for electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All agency documents must have a valid signature, including those sent through the webportal. OFR will only accept documents signed with a medium assurance level digital signature certificate, cross-certified by the Federal Bridge Certification Authority in PKCS#7 open standard (PKI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most federal HSPD-12 PIV cards meet this level. The name in the signature block must meet PKI name-matching requirements (see Table 1-2). Agencies may use a digital autopen; deviations to signature-block/name matching require a formal deviation request (Appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature block name-matching rules (digital)
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature block must match the signer’s full name as it appears in the digital signature with limited exceptions: first name may be shown in full or as an initial; middle/maiden name may be added or dropped but first name cannot be dropped; cannot add a first name or use a nickname not in the digital signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 1-2 provides valid examples (e.g., Digital Signature 'Cynthia James' allows signature blocks like 'C. James', 'Cynthia Ann James', etc.). To use a non-conforming signature-block form, submit a formal deviation request including exact form of digital signature and preferred non-compliant signature-block name with justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A signature date is recommended but not required. If used, the signature date should be the date of actual signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postdated signatures are not accepted and OFR will not change a signature date. If the date is more than 3 months old, OFR will add an editorial note indicating when it actually received the document. If the date is more than 12 months old or there is another problem with the date, OFR will remove the document from the production process and make it available for pick-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of signature block in paper documents
rubrics_metrics.description: You may place the signature block either at the end of the document or between the preamble and the rest of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In joint documents that require multiple signatures, do not separate the signatures. If all agencies sign at the end of regulatory text, contact the Scheduling Unit for the best way to prepare signature pages (see Example 1-12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Webportal (digital transmission) preferred and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register Document Submission Portal (webportal) lets agencies securely transmit documents and special handling letters online and receive immediate status feedback. Using the webportal is strongly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All rules for drafting documents apply to digitally signed and webportal-submitted documents. For details on online transmission procedures and how to obtain a digital signature, see Chapter 6 and Appendix B (PKI and Digital Signature FAQs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper transmission fallback and required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If unable to send electronically, agencies may send paper documents: one original paper document (with a wet signature) plus a CD containing the MS Word file that is an exact duplicate of the signed paper document, and a letter certifying the Word file is an exact duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot send the MS Word file on a CD, contact OFR to discuss electronic signatures. Note it can take up to one business day to add a paper document with CD to the production system (account for extra processing time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Rules category must-include items
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents published in the Proposed Rules category must include: Document Headings; Preamble; List of Subjects (for documents with proposed regulatory text); Words of Issuance (for documents with proposed regulatory text); a description of the proposed changes or the proposed regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are in addition to general Chapter 1 requirements. Legal authorities cited include 1 CFR 5.9 and 1 CFR parts 18, 21, and 22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble content restrictions and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed-rule document must contain a preamble that explains the basis and purpose of the proposed regulatory text but contains no regulatory text. It arranges basic information on the who, what, where, when, and why of a document for the reader’s convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include quotations of regulatory or statutory text in the preamble (see section 2.6). Footnotes and endnotes are only permitted within SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings format for proposed rule documents (CFR citation, docket, RIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headings of a proposed rule document must identify the CFR title and part your document proposes to amend or relates to, and present headings using the appropriate format (with subagency vs without).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the CFR citation (part number even if only one paragraph is affected or full chapter), include your agency docket number if you have one, and include the RIN if you have one (RIN assigned by RISC and determined in consultation with OMB). OFR does not determine whether you need or have a docket number or RIN.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR citation inclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFR citation contains the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document proposes to amend or is directly related to. Even if the document affects only one paragraph within a part, include that part number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include the full chapter number in place of specific parts. Examples of proper citation format provided in Chapter 2 and Appendix examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency docket number inclusion rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency docket number is your agency’s internal file number. If you have an agency docket number, you must include it in the heading as shown in examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions about docket numbers, speak with your agency; OFR does not know if you have one or need one.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIN inclusion and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulation Identifier Number (RIN) is assigned by the Regulatory Information Service Center and identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda. If you have a RIN, you must include it in the heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your agency, in consultation with OMB, determines whether you need a RIN. OFR does not determine RIN assignment.
